h1: PROMPT — Agencies & Studios Hero Section Design
tagline: Hero section reference for an agency or studio, captured at 1472x1080 with the layout, timings and palette specified in the brief.
summary: Hero section reference for an agency or studio — Inter Tight, 80ms transitions, a stats row and a dark stage.
about: PROMPT keeps its decision trail: the brief that produced this hero section runs 13,186 characters. Colour is limited to black #000000 underneath and white #FFFFFF for the type, set in Inter Tight. The reference is built with React and Tailwind CSS, and the layout decisions are stated independently of it. Motion is limited to 80ms transitions and a looping video bed. Keep it open while you write: the 13,186-character brief is the part that transfers to your own page.

layout.title: Links collapse at one width
layout.body: The bar is one row of text and one action, measured at 100vh sections and 32px spacing steps so it reads as a strip rather than as a band. The bar sits over the 1472x1080 composition without a background of its own, so the media runs edge to edge underneath it.

layout.title: Cards without borders
layout.body: The grid is the structure: panels of the same size, set in Inter Tight, arranged so the eye moves across rather than down. Panel heights are driven by the copy, so a longer line does not break the alignment of the row.

layout.title: Top row, one action
layout.body: Give the wordmark no more room than its type needs. The reference was captured at 1472x1080.

layout.title: Numbers carried into the build
layout.body: Nothing in the layout is left to feel: the brief quotes 100vh sections, 32px spacing steps and 80ms transitions and the build has to hit those values. There is no invented intermediate value between the named ones; the measurement list is the whole system.

motion.title: It respects reduced-motion
motion.body: The motion layer has an off switch. Under prefers-reduced-motion, the entrance and the loop is dropped and everything else stays where it is. With reduced motion on, the composition holds its final state rather than snapping mid-transition.

motion.title: Fast enough to feel deliberate
motion.body: The animation budget is small and explicit: 80ms, applied to state changes rather than to entrances. The same duration is reused across controls, which keeps the interactions feeling like one system.

fonts.name: Inter Tight
fonts.weights: Weight not fixed in the brief
fonts.role: Headline and interface text — one face for the whole page

editorial.title: Why this composition works for agency
editorial.body: The trade-off is density: this hero section says less on the first screen than a feature-led layout would. What it keeps is the reading order, and navigation, the announcement badge, the stats row, the card grid and the feature list do the work a longer page would spread out. It gives a agency reader the shortest honest route to the offer.

editorial.title: How PROMPT sequences the first read
editorial.body: The brief runs 13,186 characters and names the reading order explicitly: navigation, the announcement badge, the stats row, the card grid and the feature list, with 100vh sections and 32px spacing steps between them. A agency reader gets the offer before the options.

editorial.title: How the hero section reflows
editorial.body: Wide, the composition is dense; narrow, the section is held at 100vh, the navigation collapses into a mobile menu and the motion has a reduced-motion branch. Both states are described in the brief. Width changes the measurements, not the reading path.

faq.question: What do I get when I copy the PROMPT brief?
faq.answer: The captured brief runs 13,186 characters and covers the frame, the type scale, the palette and the transitions. Copying it gives you that text, and sending it to Studio stages the same request with the page already described.

faq.question: Can I rebuild the PROMPT hero section in a different stack?
faq.answer: PROMPT was built in React and Tailwind CSS, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

faq.question: What drives the motion in PROMPT?
faq.answer: Transitions are attached to interface states rather than to a scroll timeline, and they resolve in the 80ms range. The brief records the values so a port can match them without guessing.
